source_title: Cardinals pick concessionaire for new ballpark
body_text:
The Cardinals said Tuesday that Aramark Corp. will run concessions at the new Busch
Stadium when it opens for the 2006 season, ending a four-decade run by Sportservice at
the old park. The 10-year deal is worth about $30 million over its life, according to two
people briefed on the terms who spoke on condition of anonymity because the contract has
not been made public.

Levy Restaurants and Centerplate also bid for the work. Team officials said the decision
turned on Aramark's proposal for the club level rather than on price alone.

Roughly 200 concession workers at Coors Field walked off the job before Sunday's game,
the second work stoppage this season against Aramark, the company that has held the
stadium's food service contract for years. The union said the dispute is over health
coverage for part-time staff, most of whom work fewer than twenty games a season.

An Aramark spokeswoman said the company was disappointed and that stands would remain
open with management staffing them. The Rockies declined to comment on the contract.

Several vendors were named this week for the retail spaces adjoining the ballpark. A
spokesman said the leases run through the end of the decade and that further tenants
would be announced once the second phase of construction is financed and under way. No
food service contractor for the stadium itself was named in the announcement, and the
team declined to say whether the existing agreement would be extended.

source_publication: St. Louis Business Journal; St. Louis, Mo.
source_title: Delaware North takes over Busch Stadium concessions
body_text:
Delaware North's Sportservice unit will take over food and beverage service at
Busch Stadium beginning with the 2019 season, the Cardinals confirmed Monday, replacing
Aramark after thirteen years. Terms were not disclosed. The club said the change had been
under discussion since the previous fall and that most hourly staff would be retained.

Sportservice ran concessions at the old Busch Stadium until 2005, so the award returns the
company to a ballpark it left fourteen years ago. An Aramark spokesman said the company
was proud of its work in St. Louis and would continue to serve other Missouri accounts.

source_title: Dining workers at Whitmore College ratify first contract
body_text:
Dining hall workers at Whitmore College have ratified their first contract with
Compass Group, the company that has run food service on the campus since the college
outsourced its dining halls. The three-year agreement raises the starting wage and adds
paid sick leave for workers who average more than twenty hours a week during the term.

The college declined to say what it pays Compass. A spokeswoman said the arrangement had
been in place long enough that the college no longer maintained its own kitchen staff.

source_title: Padres award Petco Park food contract to Sodexo
body_text:
The Padres have awarded the concessions contract at Petco Park to Sodexo, the club
    said Monday, ending a run by the previous operator that began when the ballpark opened.
    The agreement runs seven years with an option for three more, and takes effect at the
    start of the 2025 season.

Sodexo said it would keep the ballpark's local-vendor program and add a commissary
    on the east side of the park. The club would not say what the contract is worth.
